entities.summary:
Sebastian z Felsztyna was a prominent Polish composer and music theorist of the early 16th century, who played a pivotal role in shaping the country's musical identity during the Renaissance.


 Born into a noble family in 1500s Poland, Sebastian z Felsztyna's expertise in music theory and composition was shaped by the cultural influences of the time, including the works of Italian composers like Palestrina.


 His most notable compositions, including the 'Missa de Beata Maria Virgine' and 'Missa in C minor', showcased his mastery of Renaissance polyphony and his ability to blend traditional Polish folk music with European styles.


 Sebastian z Felsztyna's legacy extended beyond his own compositions, as his music theories and compositions influenced generations of Polish composers, including the famous composer, Jan Lewycki.


 Today, Sebastian z Felsztyna is remembered as one of the greatest Polish composers of the early 16th century, whose contributions to the development of Polish music continue to be celebrated and performed around the world.
